notes: PWASI 2026 is a Government of Ghana / Ghana Scholarships Authority regional scheme (scholarships.gov.gh). Official notice fetched 2026-10-14: 'The Government of Republic of Ghana is offering scholarships for full-time, on campus undergraduate and postgraduate studies in Public Tertiary Education Institutions in Ghana to qualified students from ECOWAS member states.' The notice attaches only a list of 18 participating public tertiary institutions (University of Ghana, KNUST, UCC, UDS, UHAS, UENR, ATU, KTU, TTU, HTU, UMaT, UESD, UBIDS, UTAS, USTED, GIMPA, UEW, UniMAC) with admission-application links; no supervising professor, programme faculty or research group is named. Applications go to the GSA portal and, separately, to the universities' own admissions; nomination is by ECOWAS nominating agencies. No institution or supervisor is attached to the scheme itself.

Study in Saudi (studyinsaudi.sa, Ministry of Education platform) Visa Options page fetched 2026-10-14. The page only describes visa pathways and three funding tiers ('Tuition, housing & living - all covered' Full Scholarships; Partial Scholarships; Paid Study Programs). Acceptance is 'from a licensed and accredited educational institution in the Kingdom' and applications are made through the institution of choice via the platform; no individual institution, supervisor or faculty is attached to this national government scholarship listing.

PAU scholarship is a central African Union Commission scheme (au.int announcement, plus au-pau.org/submission application portal fetched 2026-10-14). Announcement: 'The African Union Commission will offer full scholarships to successful candidates.' Applicants apply online at au-pau.org/submission for master's/PhD places at any of the four PAU institutes (PAUSTI at JKUAT Kenya; PAUGHSS at Universite de Yaounde II Cameroon; PAUWES at Abou Bekr Belkaid University Tlemcen Algeria; PAULESI at University of Ibadan Nigeria); the call names no supervisors and admission/placement is decided centrally by PAU/AUC, analogous to central Erasmus Mundus. No supervising professor is tied to the scholarship itself.

Turkiye Scholarships (Turkiye Burslari) is a central government programme of the Presidency of Turks Abroad and Related Communities (YTB). Official 2026 announcement fetched 2026-10-14: it 'provides university placement and academic, social and cultural facilities to its awardees at all levels of higher education' - i.e. YTB assigns the university placement for associate, bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees (application window 10 January-20 February 2026, tbbs.turkiyeburslari.gov.tr). The announcement and programme site name no supervising professor, faculty or host lab.

World in Serbia Project is a Ministry of Education, Science and Technological Development of the Republic of Serbia government scheme (prosveta.gov.rs PDF call for 2026/2027-2028). It funds free study at Serbian public higher education institutions in all programmes and levels after a preparatory Serbian-language year, for candidates from Non-Aligned Movement member/observer states. The scheme is run and awarded by the Ministry; no institution, supervisor or faculty is attached to the award, and applicants are not required to secure a supervisor when applying.

PTDF Overseas Postgraduate Scholarship Scheme is run by the Petroleum Technology Development Fund, a Nigerian federal agency (scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng notice, posted 18 January 2026; fetched 2026-10-14). Applications are made through the PTDF Scholarship Management Portal for approved programmes at several partner universities in the UK, Germany, France and Malaysia (2026 UK PhD split-site partners named: Robert Gordon University, University of Strathclyde, University of Portsmouth, with CPESK Kaduna). The notice states only that 'Applicants intending to pursue a PhD scholarship under the PTDF/DAAD partnership in Germany are required to secure a research supervisor prior to the final selection interviews' - no specific supervisor is published or attached to the scheme; supervisors are arranged individually by candidates after selection.

Cusanuswerk Promotionsstipendium (cusanuswerk.de/en/bewerbung/promovierende/promotion, fetched 2026-10-14) is a talent-development body scholarship of the Catholic Church in Germany, not an institution-attached programme. Doctoral candidates apply with their own research expose and must already hold admission to a doctorate (for foreign applicants: 'Zulassung zur Promotion an einer staatlich anerkannten Hochschule in Deutschland'), so the supervisor depends on the candidate's own chosen university and is not tied to the scholarship. The only named contacts on the page - Dr. habil. Jan Christoph Suntrup and Dr. Tobias Davids (Cusanuswerk Auswahlverfahren officers, Auswahl-Prom@cusanuswerk.de) - are selection-process staff of the funding body, not supervising professors, so no professor entries are recorded.
